title: ComEd FERC OATT Attachment H-13 take-or-pay floor
statement: A ten-year FERC-jurisdictional Transmission Security Agreement guaranteeing that annual PJM transmission payments under OATT Attachment H-13 do not fall below what the submitted load ramp implies, with any shortfall recovered from the customer. It is the single largest UNPRICED item in this project and it carries no dollar figure here, which is the point.

title: Substation and interconnection capex transfer
statement: Every voltage sibling is priced against an UNPRICED transfer of substation and interconnection capex onto the customer. It is stated wherever a sibling appears and it is in no total.

title: Retail schedules stand proxy for a >100 MW contract
statement: A giga-scale campus exceeds every published retail schedule in the library. The largest published schedule is used as a documented proxy for a negotiated large-load contract, and the negotiated contract is what a real campus would sign.

title: Three voltage siblings, priced and deliberately EXCLUDED
statement: M-COL-VOLT, M-DFW-VOLT and M-SJ-VOLT are BASELINE-SIDE: the published baseline is already billed on the higher-voltage schedule. Counting them again would overstate the mitigation by 2.7x the entire real stack. They are shown as an excluded band, never as an absence.

title: PG&E Option R is unavailable to a load of this shape
statement: The modelled battery is 8.32 % of the 1,201,596 kW facility peak against an eligibility floor of 20 %. Priced anyway it is a net LOSS, and the dominant term is the shared energy uplift rather than the demand structure.

title: PG&E Option S is unavailable to a load of this shape
statement: Against a 10 % floor, and Option S's smallest qualifying system is 2.403x the entire 50 MW B-20 programme cap - unreachable by construction, and barred on day one at a new location by the sheet's own words.

title: ComEd Rate BESH: the WINDOW is ruled, the ZONAL SCALING FACTOR is not (Chicago pair)
statement: P6-R10 ADOPTED the derived_uniform coincident-peak window, so the half of F4C-7 that was about the window is discharged. What keeps the row open is the OTHER half: the PLC is a 5CP average times a zonal scaling factor, and no source this project has read publishes ComEd's ZSF, so every Chicago figure stands at ZSF = 1.000 by assumption. Chicago publishes as a PAIR until the ZSF is sourced. This is an EPISTEMIC bracket (F6E-2): it has no expiry, because what is missing is a fact about the world.

title: Dominion GS-4's three demand quantities are RULED; the engine cannot yet bill them (Northern Virginia pair)
statement: Northern Virginia publishes as a pair. The primary figure is what this project's billing engine bills from its database. The alternative, 92.6193 $ per IT-MWh, is what Dominion Schedule GS-4 bills: the tariff's three demand quantities - Distribution Demand under a 100 % twelve-month ratchet, On-Peak Electricity Supply Demand under a 75 % summer-anchored ratchet, and Off-Peak Electricity Supply Demand as the excess over 90 % of the on-peak quantity - priced from the paragraphs themselves. The 5.1473 $ per IT-MWh gap is a limitation of this project's billing engine, not an uncertainty about the tariff. It closes when schema v1.5 gives the schedule three billing determinants and a per-determinant ratchet, at which point this metro publishes a single figure. This is a MODELLING bracket (F6E-2) and its due date is Unit 6F.

title: Chicago's PJM coincident-peak window is DERIVED and carries two named residuals
statement: Chicago's PJM coincident-peak window is DERIVED from 22 observations of the PJM RTO annual summer peak hour (2025 State of the Market Report for PJM, Section 3, Table 3-6) and carries two named residuals: the zonal scaling factor is unsourced, so every figure is unscaled (ZSF = 1.000); and the source tabulates the annual peak hour, not the five-day 5CP candidate set. The window is June-August, 14:00-17:00 Chicago prevailing, weekdays - and the weekday restriction is EMPIRICAL here (22 of 22 observations), where ERCOT's 4CP weekday restriction is ASSUMED, with cp4_kw_allday reported beside it as the sensitivity. The two coincident peaks are not one method.

title: The two-segment PUE overlay: the chord bias is REMOVED, and what the form does not see
direction: no longer an upper bound in this channel
statement: SUPERSEDED, with record. Above the 25.556 C design wet bulb the economiser is fully out and the only remaining channel is the chiller's own 1.5 %/F. Through Unit 6E-1 these extracts carried a single CHORD across the whole range, which OVERSTATED PUE above the design point by up to 0.0184 at Phoenix, 0.0171 at Austin and 0.0122 at Dallas-Fort Worth - at the interval that sets the demand charge in five of eight metros - so every figure was an upper bound in that channel. These extracts are on the two_segment_ph6 form, which prices that range at a marginal 0.00198 PUE/C against the chord's 0.00471, and the bias is gone. What the form does NOT see, stated rather than narrated away: its acceptance gate reads only each metro's single hottest interval and is blind to the shape of the correction between the design point and the maximum; and nothing in the form prices a tariff - the dollar effect is Unit 4E's measurement. The form MOVES THE BILLED PEAK INTERVAL in three of eight metros (Atlanta, Austin and Northern Virginia) and leaves the metro order unchanged at every bracket-end combination.

title: The alpha elasticity domain, and the bound Unit 4A still enforces
statement: Unit 2F published 4.947 at its own reporting level L = 1.20. On the LINEAR form at the ruled L = 1.150 the same construction gives 4.7405. On the two_segment_ph6 form these extracts are published on it WIDENS to 5.4014, and that is the figure in pue_alpha_domain_max. Unit 4A is not edited, so 4A's own emission gate still bounds alpha by the LINEAR 4.7405 while emitting two-segment series: it enforces the TIGHTER of the two and refuses more than it must, never less (F6E-7). The operative alpha is 2.8311 and it is inside both.

title: The +/-25 % market bands, and the one adjacency they touch
statement: The three CHEAPEST metros are exactly the three banded ones, so the top of the ranking is its least certain part. Columbus's upper edge crosses Chicago's central, and that pair is the ONLY adjacency the bands touch anywhere in the table. THE SIZE OF THE CROSSING DEPENDS ON THE BASIS: 0.9742 $/MWh on the Phase 2 METERED basis, which is the 0.97 era_ph2_report_v1.2.md publishes, against 0.8179 $/MWh on the PUBLISHED FACILITY basis these extracts are on. A view built on G1 must quote the facility figure. Both parameters now come from one table and one statistic, so moving them independently is not a scenario that can happen.

title: Atlanta and Phoenix are a LIBRARY GAP, not a tariff finding
statement: Georgia Power's and APS's tariff books have not been read for electives with the thoroughness ComEd's and Dominion's have. That is a statement about this project's reading, not about those tariffs. It cannot move the order.

title: PG&E Peak Day Pricing is absent from the library
statement: Worth $32.48/kW-yr of summer demand credit against a $0.90/kWh event charge. It is the ONLY elective in the library that is a RISK TRADE and could go the wrong way for an uncurtailable load.

title: Dallas-Fort Worth's parameter deserves less confidence
statement: ERCOT North's implied load-weighting premium is +0.198 % against a PJM minimum of +5.72 %. Either the corroborating annual figure is itself load-weighted - in which case parity is already broken inside DFW's own source - or ERCOT North's 2025 duration curve really was that flat. Re-targeting to $35.34/MWh was priced and declined.

title: M-SJ-PF is a CORRECTION, not an election
statement: San Jose reads 0.70 $/metered-MWh high because the engine does not evaluate a mechanic the database holds. It is in the mitigated stack on that footing, not as a tariff election the customer chooses.

title: The recorded Ohio kWh excise figure was wrong by 1.95x
statement: The published stack carries the DERIVED value, not the recorded estimate. An estimate flagged as one is a debt, and it came due.

title: The Ohio statutory liability has no monthly form and G3 ALLOCATES it
statement: ORC 5727.81(C) is an ANNUAL self-assessment with an annual 500 GWh tier breakpoint and an annual per-location fee. G3 spreads it across the twelve months on the month's share of metered kWh. The annual total is exact; the monthly split is a DECLARED ALLOCATION and the only one in the four grains.

title: The map point is a weather STATION, not a site
statement: G1's station_latitude and station_longitude are read from the metro's own EPW LOCATION line - the station this project's PUE overlay is driven by. No site has been chosen in any metro and the columns are named so that they cannot be read as one.

title: The PG&E instrument question is DISCHARGED on eligibility
statement: Closed on eligibility rather than on value: the advertised storage tariff does not reach a load this size. That is a siting finding, not a gap.

title: DCT-T's inert ratchet is DISCHARGED on measurement
statement: $0.00 measured four times. DCT-T's 85 % capacity floor is 1,040,584 kW against a lowest monthly 30-minute peak of 1,140,126 kW - 99,542 kW of headroom - and the floor is anchored on a CONTRACT, so shaving the peak does not move it.
